doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Musicians moving to the Lower East Side
summary: As clubs like the Tin Palace and Five Spot appeared, musicians including Ed Blackwell moved downtown.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That was – talk about some of the other people that – beyond the musicians’ circle – well, first of all, when did musicians start to come to the Lower East Side?

This is what I was saying. They started migrating down that way when the scene began to evolve down that way, because then another joint opened up over further, the Tin Palace or some other place, and another place somewhere else. Then sometimes I’d go across and work at the Vanguard. Max would call me – Max Gordon. I’d go over there and work with him. So Slug’s became a real spot.
Was the Five Spot part of that? The Dome part of that?
Yeah, all those clubs. It’s just another – that was the scene.
Who do you remember coming? Because that came to be associated with, I think, maybe a lot of avant garde players.
Yeah, [Ed] Blackwell and a whole lot of guys began to move down that part of town. I can’t remember everybody. But there was a lot of people down there.
